newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg buys car component maker Yale-South Haven.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg buys car component maker Yale-South Haven.

text.p: Swedish mining and rubber group Trelleborg AB said Tuesday that its Trelleborg Industri unit purchased Yale-South Haven Inc. of South Haven, Mich.
No financial details on the deal were given.

Yale-South Haven, which has five factories in the United States and Mexico with 900 employees, manufactures anti-vibration components for auto manufacturers, including General Motors Corp., Chrysler Corp and Ford Motor Co.
"The acquisition is a link in our aspiration to be one of the leading players in the world in vibration-dampening components for the car industry," Trelleborg Managing Director Kjell Nilsson said.
He said by combining resources in Trelleborg Automotive, the companies would meet the vehicle industry's demand for increased services from subcontractors.
Nilsson said Trelleborg Industri and Yale-South Haven had worked closely in Europe and North America since 1994.
